checks_performed: Created verify_counterexample.py in the writable scratch directory. It directly enumerates every ordered pair (x,y) with x+y≤22m and evaluates all three colors.
Exhaustively checked m=1,...,80. In every case the direct counts matched R_mixed=60m², R_odd-odd=39m²+3m, and R_total=99m²+3m.
Used exact rational arithmetic to verify in every checked case that the density exceeds 9/22, hence also exceeds 2/5+1/220. For m=80 the reduced density was 7923/19349.
final_writeup:
The proposed upper bound is false.

For every positive integer m, put n=22m and define c:[n]→{1,2,3} by

c(k)=1 if k is even;
c(k)=2 if k is odd and either k≤8m or k>20m;
c(k)=3 if k is odd and 8m<k≤20m.

There are 11m even integers. Among the odds, color 2 occurs on the 4m odds below 8m and the m odds above 20m, hence on 5m integers total; color 3 occurs on the remaining 6m odds.

First consider triples having one odd and one even addend. Choosing any color-2 odd u and color-3 odd v, let a=min(u,v), z=max(u,v), and e=z−a. Then e is a positive even integer and a+e=z, so (a,e,z) and (e,a,z) are rainbow. Conversely, every rainbow triple with mixed-parity addends arises uniquely this way. Thus these triples contribute 2(5m)(6m)=60m².

If both addends are odd, their sum is even and therefore has color 1. Such a triple is rainbow precisely when one addend has color 2 and the other color 3. A color-2 odd above 20m cannot occur here, since its sum with the smallest color-3 odd is greater than 22m. Write the remaining possible addends as

2i−1,  1≤i≤4m,
and
8m+2j−1,  1≤j≤6m.

Their sum is at most 22m exactly when i+j≤7m+1. The number of unoriented pairs is

6m(m+1)+Σ_{i=m+2}^{4m}(7m+1−i)
=6m(m+1)+(3m−1)(9m)/2
=(39m²+3m)/2.

Each has two orientations, so odd-odd addends contribute 39m²+3m ordered triples. Two even addends can never give a rainbow triple. Consequently

R_m=99m²+3m.

Since the total number of ordered Schur triples is

binom(22m,2)=242m²−11m,

the rainbow density is

R_m/binom(22m,2)=(99m+3)/(242m−11)>99/242=9/22.

Finally, 9/22=90/220 while 2/5+1/220=89/220. Taking ε=1/220, every member n=22m of this unbounded sequence violates the asserted upper bound. Hence no corresponding N exists.

results.claim: For n=22m, the stated coloring has 11m even color-1 elements, 5m odd color-2 elements, and 6m odd color-3 elements.
results.proof_sketch: The odds at most 8m number 4m; the odds strictly above 20m and at most 22m number m. These receive color 2. The intervening odd block contains 6m elements and receives color 3. All 11m evens receive color 1.

results.claim: Rainbow triples with one even and one odd addend are in two-to-one correspondence with pairs consisting of one color-2 odd and one color-3 odd.
results.proof_sketch: For differently colored odds u<v, the positive difference v−u is even and has color 1, giving the two ordered triples (u,v−u,v) and (v−u,u,v). Conversely, in a mixed-parity rainbow triple, the even entry has color 1 and the odd addend and odd sum must have colors 2 and 3. Their difference recovers the even addend, so the correspondence is exact.

results.claim: The number of mixed-parity ordered rainbow triples is 60m².
results.proof_sketch: There are (5m)(6m)=30m² cross-color pairs of odds. Each yields exactly two ordered triples by the preceding correspondence.

results.claim: The number of odd-odd ordered rainbow triples is 39m²+3m.
results.proof_sketch: The high color-2 odd block cannot participate because even its smallest possible sum with the color-3 block exceeds 22m. Parameterizing the low color-2 and color-3 odds by 2i−1 and 8m+2j−1 gives i+j≤7m+1. Summing the permitted j gives (39m²+3m)/2 unordered pairs, each with two orientations.

results.claim: The coloring has exactly 99m²+3m ordered rainbow Schur triples.
results.proof_sketch: Add the 60m² mixed-parity triples and 39m²+3m odd-odd triples. Even-even triples have two entries of color 1 and are never rainbow.

results.claim: This sequence has limiting rainbow density 9/22 and refutes the target with ε=1/220.
results.proof_sketch: Division by binom(22m,2)=242m²−11m gives (99m+3)/(242m−11)>99/242=9/22. Since 9/22=90/220>89/220=2/5+1/220, arbitrarily large n=22m violate the claimed bound.
